AK.key_factor: Peltola led every nonpartisan poll since September, but the late spoiler-candidate scandal and two criminal probes land in the final week of a ranked-choice race she needs to win outright.
AK.reasoning: Peltola won the primary 49.5-41.4 and holds a 2-7 point lead in Siena and Alaska Survey Research polls, backed by a 2.5-to-1 fundraising edge. Ranked-choice transfers from Sullivan Jr. and Heikes voters favor the incumbent, and the Oct 28 spoiler-recruitment story plus state and federal investigations give Sullivan a late argument. Trump at 37% approval and a D+9 generic ballot keep Peltola narrowly ahead.

FL.key_factor: Moody leads every poll since September, most by 4-10 points, in a state with a 1.5 million Republican registration edge.
FL.reasoning: Florida went R+13 in 2024 and only Democratic-sponsored polls show the race within two points. Nixon's DSA affiliation limits crossover appeal in a state that gave DeSantis a 19-point win in 2022. Heavy Democratic outside spending and the wave environment compress the margin to the mid-single digits, but Moody's registration advantage and consistent polling lead make an upset unlikely.

IA.key_factor: Nonpartisan polls show Turek up about a point, but Iowa polling overstated Democrats in 2020 and 2024 in a state that went R+13.
IA.reasoning: Polls split almost evenly: YouGov, Marist, Suffolk and Fox show Turek ahead while Emerson, CNN, Siena and Republican pollsters show Hinson narrowly ahead. Turek enjoys a large money advantage and a D+9 national environment, which offsets most of Iowa's Republican lean. The state's recent pattern of Republican overperformance versus polls tips a genuine coin flip slightly toward Hinson, with the Libertarian drawing a few points.

KS.key_factor: Every nonpartisan poll in late October shows Hamilton ahead, by 3 to 9 points, after the patient-lawsuit revelations and Trump's slur at a Marshall rally.
KS.reasoning: Kansas is R+16 but elected Democrat Laura Kelly governor twice, and Hamilton, a megachurch pastor, fits the crossover profile. He has outraised Marshall nearly 3-to-1, and Emerson, Washington Post, CNN and YouGov all show him leading. Marshall's lawsuits against patients and the redirected Senate Leadership Fund money signal Republican alarm. The state's deep partisan lean keeps this close, but the evidence favors Hamilton.

ME.key_factor: Jackson leads most October polls by 2-4 points in a D+7 state while Trump sits near 37% approval, though Collins beat her 2020 polls by roughly 13 points.
ME.reasoning: Collins is the only Republican senator from a state Trump never carried, and the ProPublica pay-to-play story adds a late liability. CNN, Marist, Suffolk, Washington Post and the Fox registered-voter sample all show Jackson ahead; only Republican-sponsored polls show ties. Collins' history of outperforming polls and her appropriations clout justify real uncertainty, but a D+9 national environment is far worse for her than 2020.

MI.key_factor: El-Sayed leads nearly every October poll by 2-8 points, and Rogers lost in 2024 even with Trump carrying the state.
MI.reasoning: Rogers fell short by 0.3 points in a presidential year that was R+1.4 in Michigan. A midterm with Trump at 37% approval and a D+9 generic ballot removes his best turnout conditions. Glengariff, Mitchell, Marist and MSU polls show El-Sayed up 5-8; only partisan Republican polls show a near-tie. Republican outside spending of $35 million and AIPAC-linked mailers keep it competitive but not a toss-up.

MN.key_factor: Flanagan leads every poll since mid-September, including Siena by 14 and SurveyUSA by 7, in a D+4 state during a Democratic wave.
MN.reasoning: Minnesota has not elected a Republican to the Senate since 2002, and Tafoya is a first-time candidate carrying a Trump endorsement in a state where he is deeply unpopular. Flanagan won the DFL primary comfortably and holds the lieutenant governor's statewide profile. Tafoya's fundraising edge is modest. The main uncertainty is margin, not the winner, with minor candidates taking a few points.

NC.key_factor: Cooper leads every poll by 8-14 points, outraised Whatley nearly 4-to-1, and the Senate Leadership Fund pulled $30 million from the race.
NC.reasoning: Cooper is a two-term governor who won statewide six times and faces a former party chair with no electoral record. Early voting shows Democratic-registered voters far ahead of Republicans, and national Republicans have effectively conceded by redirecting money to Kansas. Even allowing for North Carolina's R+3 lean and past polling misses, double-digit leads across pollsters of all types make this the safest Democratic pickup.

NE.key_factor: Osborn's own campaign poll shows him trailing by two, and his 2024 polls similarly showed a tight race before he lost by nearly seven.
NE.reasoning: Osborn's independent populist brand keeps the race within the margin in most surveys, with YouGov and a Democratic PAC poll showing him narrowly ahead. But Nebraska is R+20, Ricketts won the 2024 special with 62.6%, Trump campaigned for him, and Republican pollsters show Ricketts up 3-5. The 2024 precedent of Osborn underperforming his polls argues for Ricketts winning by low-to-mid single digits.

NH.key_factor: Pappas has led every poll since mid-September by 5-8 points, including Republican-sponsored surveys.
NH.reasoning: New Hampshire has not elected a Republican senator since Sununu himself in 2002, and he lost to Shaheen by 6 in 2008. Pappas has outraised him 4-to-1 and holds steady leads from Saint Anselm, UNH, Siena and YouGov. Sununu's family name and heavy outside spending keep Republicans within striking distance, but no poll shows him ahead. Trump at 37% approval seals the lean toward Pappas.

OH.key_factor: Brown leads most nonpartisan polls by 3-6 points, and in 2024 he lost by only 3.6 while Trump carried Ohio by 11.
OH.reasoning: A midterm with a D+9 generic ballot removes the presidential coattails that sank Brown two years ago. Fox, Marist, YouGov, Siena, Suffolk and CNN all show him ahead; only Rasmussen and co/efficient give Husted a slim lead. Brown has raised $68 million against Husted's $20 million. Ohio polls overstated Brown in 2024 by about three points, which keeps Husted close, but the data favor Brown narrowly.

SC.key_factor: Most nonpartisan polls show Graham ahead by 1-4 points in a state that went R+18, with Siena's tie the main outlier.
SC.reasoning: Graham is an unusual nominee, appointed after her brother's death and winning the runoff narrowly, and Andrews has outraised her 12-to-1. That explains why polls are far closer than South Carolina's partisanship implies. But ECU, Trafalgar, Targoz, Citadel and Rasmussen all show Graham leading, and only Democratic-sponsored polls show Andrews ahead. Record early turnout in a deep-red state is likelier to favor the Republican.

TX.key_factor: Talarico leads most nonpartisan polls by 2-6 points, but Texas polls overstated Democrats by 3-5 points in 2020, 2022 and 2024.
TX.reasoning: Paxton is a scandal-plagued nominee who refused all debates and has been outspent roughly 7-to-1 by a candidate who raised $146 million. The national environment is worse for Republicans than in 2018, when Cruz won by only 2.6. Siena, YouGov, UT and University of Houston show Talarico ahead; Republican pollsters show a tie. A 600,000-application registration backlog and Texas' R+14 lean keep this a true toss-up.

upset_watch.why: Paxton trails by only a couple of points in a state whose polls have overstated Democrats in three straight cycles, so a modest Republican polling error would hand him the seat.
